_readme: benarbejde/asset_manifest.json -- Example Music Limited -- fetch-on-demand manifest for
bootstrap/web/ boot assets that have a real upstream, instead of vendoring them into git.
Consumed by bootstrap/setup-workstation-linux.sh, bootstrap/setup-workstation-macos.sh, and
bootstrap/Setup-Workstation.ps1. Every dest path is relative to bootstrap/web/. Nothing in
here is auto-run by the harness (at_have_ryggen_fri/check_bootstrap_assets.py stays
read-only, offline) -- fetching is always an explicit, separate script run.
Arch Linux, Rocky Linux, and Ubuntu (Alpine dd-writer) menu.ipxe entries were removed
entirely 2026-07-27 (Robert's call) -- none had real working assets (Ubuntu/Rocky had none
committed at all; Arch's own airootfs.sfs/initramfs-linux were literal placeholder stub
files, not real assets). See menu.ipxe's own v2.10 changelog entry.
The WinPE .wim is deliberately NOT here and NEVER goes in this repo at all, LFS or
otherwise -- this repo cannot redistribute it (Microsoft ADK licensing). wimboot (the loader
that streams it, github.com/ipxe/wimboot) IS fetched below -- it's GPL2, no Microsoft code
in it, unaffected. See .gitignore's matching hard exclusion.
source_type github_release: queries the GitHub Releases API fresh every run and uses the
API's own per-asset 'digest' field for checksum verification -- nothing hardcoded here to go
stale. tag 'latest' always takes whatever's newest; a literal tag (e.g. 'v2.9.0') pins to
that exact release.
source_type url_with_checksum_file: fetches checksum_file_url as text, finds the line
containing checksum_file_entry, and regex-extracts a 64-hex-char SHA256 substring from it --
format-agnostic on purpose, so it doesn't matter whether the upstream checksum file uses GNU
style ('<hash>  <path>', Debian's SHA256SUMS) or BSD style ('SHA256 (<file>) = <hash>',
OpenBSD's SHA256).
archives[]: one download serves multiple destination files via members[] -- fetched once,
not once per member. checksum_file_url/checksum_file_entry are OPTIONAL on an archives[]
entry (added 2026-07-27 for the hdt/ entry below, same format-agnostic extraction as
url_with_checksum_file) -- omit both to skip verification, as gparted's entry below still
does (pre-existing gap, not fixed in this pass: SourceForge doesn't publish a convenient
checksum file for gparted-live the way kernel.org does for syslinux).
archives[] only supports .zip extraction (unzip / Expand-Archive) -- prefer a .zip release
over .tar.xz/.tar.gz where the upstream offers a choice, rather than adding tar support to
all 3 platform scripts for one entry.
GParted Live is x86_64 only -- it has never published an arm64 build.
Changelog:
2026-07-27  Migrated from asset_manifest.yml (same schema, same verified URLs/tags/paths --
see project memory for the research trail). JSON instead of YAML so this parses
natively in bash (jq) and PowerShell (ConvertFrom-Json) without an extra
dependency -- ansible/playbooks/bootstrap_assets/fetch-assets.yml (the Ansible
playbook this replaces) is being retired since ansible-playbook cannot run
natively on Windows at all.
2026-07-27  Moved from bootstrap/asset_manifest.json to benarbejde/asset_manifest.json --
Robert's call: this is raw source-of-truth data, belongs alongside
benarbejde/'s other JSON files (ad_forest.json, address_policy.json, etc.), not
off in bootstrap/ where nothing else JSON-shaped lives. The consuming scripts
(bootstrap/setup-workstation-{linux,macos}.sh,
bootstrap/Setup-Workstation.ps1) stay in bootstrap/ -- only the data moved.
2026-07-27  Added the hdt/ archive entry (SYSLINUX 6.03 -- lpxelinux.0, hdt.c32,
libcom32.c32, libutil.c32) and dropped the earlier note about rockylinux/ being
deferred -- Rocky Linux's menu.ipxe entries were removed entirely, not deferred.
Arch/Rocky/Ubuntu removal itself needed no manifest changes -- none of those had
manifest entries (Arch = custom build, Rocky/Ubuntu = never had a fetch source).
2026-08-06  klargoring entries reworked for arm64 (PVE 9.2's own arm64 release, Robert --
https://pve.proxmox.com/wiki/Roadmap). The real upstream release
(github.com/knightmare2600/klargoring, checked live: klargoring-20260806-
trixie-4) publishes vmlinuz-amd64/vmlinuz-arm64 etc, not the old unsuffixed
'vmlinuz' this manifest previously pointed at -- that asset name no longer
exists upstream at all, so the pre-existing amd64 entries were already stale,
not just missing arm64 coverage. dest paths now match menu.ipxe v2.11's
klargoring/amd64/ + klargoring/arm64/ split. Added KERNEL_VERSION-{amd64,arm64}
too (not consumed by any code, but a real published release asset worth
keeping fetchable alongside its vmlinuz/initrd).

archives._comment: SYSLINUX 6.03 (last stable release) -- pxelinux.0's own follow-up fetches (config, .c32 modules) expect TFTP; lpxelinux.0 is SYSLINUX's HTTP-native build, matching this repo's HTTP-only web server. x86_64/BIOS only -- HDT itself is a legacy BIOS tool, no arm64 build exists. .zip release used (not .tar.xz) so the existing unzip/Expand-Archive extraction path works unmodified across all 3 platform scripts -- confirmed byte-for-byte same file layout as the .tar.xz release, just without the syslinux-6.03/ prefix directory.
